win_claim.quote: Results showed that our methods achieved highest sensitivity with competitive G-means across all imbalance degrees on both simulated and real-world datasets.

uncertain: No single main proposed method: four variants NB-Basic/NB-Tomek/NB-Comm/NB-Rec; NB-Comm chosen for 'proposed' column (best avg G-mean rank, Table 4 p.26); all four variants' values are in all_methods per row

notes: Method is undersampling (neighbourhood-based, removes majority overlap instances); SMOTE is a comparator. Per-dataset simulated results only in supplementary material on GitHub (https://github.com/fonkafon/NB-undersampling Results.git, as printed footnote 7, p.20); not fetched. Table 13 (Exp. III, SVM, p.31) lists NB variants, ENN, kmUnder, OBU, Baseline only: no SMOTE. G-mean in Table 13: Breast Cancer NB-Basic 78.83, NB-Tomek 76.1, NB-Comm 76.69, NB-Rec 79.65; MNIST 3: 94.82/94.56/94.38/77.19; MNIST 5: 96.26/96.85/95.52/70.98. Other tables: Table 3 sensitivity, 5 precision, 6 F1 (SVM, p.25-27); RF: Tables 8-11 p.28-30. Pages are PDF page index; printed page = index-1. Metric is G-mean x100 (percent).
